hints: Look at where each graph suddenly jumps up, that big jump tells you an electron is being removed from a new, closer shell.
The left graph stays low for 7 electrons then jumps at the 8th, while the right graph jumps after just 2 electrons, so work out their Group numbers.
Combine a Period 3 Group 2 metal that forms a 2+ ion with a Period 3 Group 17 non-metal that forms a 1- ion to balance the charges.
walkthrough:
**Recall what a jump means**

Think of ionisation energy as how tightly an electron is held. A small rise means same shell, a huge jump means you have started breaking into a full inner shell closer to the nucleus.

Rule: number of low energies before the jump = number of outer shell electrons = Group number (for s and p block).

**Identify the left-hand element**

The first 7 ionisation energies are low and fairly similar, then there is a huge jump to remove the 8th electron. That means 7 outer electrons.

So this is a Group 17 element in Period 3: $\text{Cl}$ which forms $\text{Cl}^{-}$.

**Identify the right-hand element**

The first 2 ionisation energies are low, then there is a clear jump to remove the 3rd electron. That means 2 outer electrons.

So this is a Group 2 element in Period 3: $\text{Mg}$ which forms $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

**Combine to make a neutral ionic compound**

To balance charge, one $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ needs two $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions.

$$\text{Mg}^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2$$

options.A: Correct. Mg is Period 3 Group 2 with 2 outer electrons, matching the jump after 2. Cl is Period 3 Group 17 with 7 outer electrons, matching the jump after 7. Mg loses 2 electrons and each Cl gains 1, giving MgCl2.
options.B: Incorrect. Ca is Group 2 and Br is Group 17, so the charges would balance as CaBr2, but neither is a Period 3 element. Ca is in Period 4 and Br is in Period 4. This traps students who match groups but ignore the Period 3 condition.
options.C: Incorrect. Na2S would need a Group 1 element (jump after 1 electron) and a Group 16 element (jump after 6 electrons). Neither graph shows those jumps, so this does not fit the data.
options.D: Incorrect. K2Se would also need a Group 1 element (jump after 1) and a Group 16 element (jump after 6). It also fails because K is in Period 4 and Se is in Period 4, not Period 3.
